name: Muse Three.js 3: training tooling (local MLX and rented GPU)
description: Adds the tooling and docs to train the Qwen3.5-4B student: token statistics to pick the sequence length, a training-data validator, an MLX path for this Mac (with an honest probe of whether mlx-lm supports Qwen3.5), a guarded RunPod runbook, and safer train_sft.py options. Ralph never trains and never rents a GPU.
standingRule: Offline-only PRD. Training runs and pod creation are manual gates. The MLX probe may `pip install mlx-lm` into .venv and read its source but must not download model weights.
manualGates: Owner runs scripts/probe_mlx.py output review, then a 200-iteration MLX smoke train before any long run
Owner approves GPU spend and runs scripts/runpod_train.sh with --yes themselves

stories.title: SFT data validator
stories.description: As the pipeline owner, I want training data checked before a run starts so that a malformed row does not crash hour three of training.
steps: Create scripts/sft_data.py (no heavy imports) with `validate_rows(rows)` returning a list of problems: every row has `prompt` (system then user) and `completion` (one assistant message), non-empty strings, no unclosed <think> tag, completion contains a fenced html block, no row with the literal text '<|im_end|>' inside.
Add `check(path)` and a CLI `python scripts/sft_data.py data/sft/train.jsonl [val.jsonl]` that prints the problem count and the first 10 problems and exits 1 when there are any.
Call it from scripts/train_sft.py before loading the model (import inside main), aborting with the report on problems.
Tests with good and bad rows for each rule.
criteria: Each of the 6 rules has a failing-row test and the clean fixture produces zero problems
train_sft.py aborts before importing torch when the data is invalid (asserted by importing the module and calling the pre-check with a bad file)

stories.title: token_stats.py: choose the sequence length
stories.description: As the pipeline owner, I want the token length distribution of the dataset so that max-len is chosen from data instead of guessed.
steps: Create scripts/token_stats.py: reads train.jsonl, counts tokens per row (prompt plus completion) with the tokenizer named by `--tokenizer` only if it is already in the local Hugging Face cache (never download); otherwise fall back to characters divided by 3.5 and label the output 'estimate'.
Print median, p90, p99, max, and the share of rows over 8192, 12288 and 16384; recommend the smallest of those covering at least 97% of rows, or say none does.
Support `--json` for machine output. Tests use the estimate path on fixture rows with known lengths.
criteria: Output states 'estimate' whenever the tokenizer was not used (asserted)
For a fixture with 100 rows of known length the recommendation matches the hand-computed value (asserted)
No test or default run touches the network

stories.title: MLX path: probe, converter and wrapper
stories.description: As the pipeline owner, I want to know honestly whether I can train the 4B student on this Mac with MLX, and have the commands ready if I can.
steps: Run `.venv/bin/pip install mlx-lm`. Create scripts/probe_mlx.py that imports mlx_lm, lists its model modules, and lists the model modules whose name contains 'qwen' and reports YES if one is named for Qwen3.5 (qwen3_5 or similar), NO if no qwen module newer than the installed Qwen3 family exists, otherwise UNKNOWN; it must not download weights or call the network, so it cannot read the model's config.json: say so and tell the owner to compare `model_type` in the Qwen3.5-4B config.json against the listed modules. Print the verdict with the evidence.

Create scripts/to_mlx.py converting data/sft/train.jsonl and val.jsonl into MLX's `{"messages": [...]}` chat format under data/mlx/ with files train.jsonl and valid.jsonl (mlx expects the name valid).
Create scripts/train_mlx.sh wrapping `mlx_lm.lora` with the args from docs/08-train-mlx.md (iterations, batch size 1, max sequence length from token_stats), refusing to run if the probe says NO.
Write docs/08-train-mlx.md with the probe result recorded as found (including 'not measured' for speed and memory) and the manual smoke command.
criteria: probe_mlx.py prints YES, NO or UNKNOWN plus its evidence, and the same verdict is written in docs/08-train-mlx.md
to_mlx.py output has train.jsonl and valid.jsonl with the messages format (asserted on fixtures)
train_mlx.sh exits non-zero with a clear message when the probe verdict is NO (asserted with a stubbed probe)

stories.title: Guarded RunPod runbook
stories.description: As the pipeline owner, I want the GPU run scripted and reviewable so that renting a pod is one deliberate command.
steps: Create scripts/runpod_train.sh: default is dry-run; it prints the exact runpodctl commands for create pod, sync repo and data, install requirements-train.txt, run train_sft.py, copy out/ back, and stop the pod, with an estimated cost line computed from `--hours` and `--rate` flags (no built-in price).
Only with `--yes` does it execute; without it, it must never call runpodctl at all. It refuses to run if data/sft/train.jsonl fails scripts/sft_data.py.

Write docs/09-train-gpu.md: when to use LoRA versus full, the per-example token estimate from token_stats, how to compute cost, how to pick a checkpoint, and the unverified items (Qwen3.5 Transformers version, throughput).
A bash test (tests/py via subprocess) checks dry-run output contains each step and that runpodctl is never invoked (put a fake runpodctl first on PATH that fails the test if called).
criteria: Dry-run prints all 6 steps and the cost line, and the fake runpodctl is never called (asserted)
Without `--yes` the script exits 0; with invalid training data it exits non-zero before any runpodctl call
docs/09-train-gpu.md states every price or throughput figure as a formula or 'not measured', never a number presented as measured

stories.title: train_sft.py: smoke mode, resume and run record
stories.description: As the pipeline owner, I want a cheap smoke run, resumable training and a record of what was run so that long runs are safe and reproducible.
steps: Add `--max-steps` (smoke), `--resume-from` (checkpoint dir) and `--seed` to scripts/train_sft.py and pass them to SFTConfig.
Write <out>/train_args.json at start with all arguments, the dataset file sizes and row counts, library versions found at runtime (guarded by try/except) and a UTC timestamp.
Move argument parsing into `parse_args(argv)` and the config assembly into `make_config(args)` that import trl lazily, so tests can call parse_args without torch installed.

Tests: parse_args defaults and overrides, the learning-rate default for lora versus full, train_args.json is written for a dry call (add `--dry-run` that writes the record and exits before loading the model).
criteria: `.venv/bin/python scripts/train_sft.py --dry-run --out <tmp>` writes train_args.json and exits 0 without importing torch (asserted by checking sys.modules in a test)
Default learning rates are 1e-4 for lora and 1e-5 for full (asserted)
docs/04-training.md documents --max-steps, --resume-from and the run record
